key_insight: A single transformer-based Riemannian flow-matching model can learn a broad slice of Standard Model collider structure directly from LHC data, spanning sub-GeV to TeV scales.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a data-driven generative approach for high-energy physics that could replace multiple specialized Monte Carlo samples with one physics-aware model.
method: Train ShellFlow on ~10^9 ATLAS 13 TeV pp collision events.
Condition on event composition and generate particles on their on-shell manifolds.
Use only two physics priors: the on-shell condition and the invariant-mass formula.
evidence_signal: From one training run, the model reproduces intra-particle kinematics, dilepton resonances (J/ψ, Υ, Z), the leptonic Weinberg angle, the W and top masses, and unseen inter-particle correlations.
watch_item: Results depend on high-volume, well-calibrated collider data and the model’s ability to preserve physical constraints during generation, which may be challenging outside the ATLAS domain.
paper_title: Learning Standard Model structure from LHC data with Riemannian flow matching
